comparison: Both address the core theoretical findings (C4-C5, C16-C17, C19-C21, C37-C38). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED with strong analytical and numerical evidence. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting major clarifications about model assumptions, more mathematical detail in main text, and finding formal arguments 'more fuzzy than need be' despite acknowledging analytical results as a 'clear strength'.

Both evaluate plasticity predictions (C22-C24, C40). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 4 with sound logical basis. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, explicitly challenging the interpretation: 'Interpreting this as a sign of more plasticity is an overstatement' and questioning whether Figure 4B is merely restating Figure 3A results.

Both address differential effects of density versus activation (C39, C71-C74, with peer also including C69). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with sound mathematical basis. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, requesting better explanation of how the model distinguishes density from activation and finding Figure 3 confusing with unclear labeling and brackets.

Both evaluate robustness claims (C25-C26). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by Figure 5 numerical calculations, acknowledging fitted rather than analytical convergence formulas. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the covariance functions tested 'are not very different' and suggesting the robustness test was not sufficiently stringent.

Both evaluate star-nosed mole empirical validation (C6, C35-C36, C41, with OpenEval also including C28-C34). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to overfitting concerns, unknown bottleneck width, block diagonal approximation, and limited data points. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, challenging the claim that full model is better given additional degrees of freedom, requesting more methodological detail, and questioning stability if outlier ray 11 is excluded.

Both address theoretical foundation and decorrelation framework (C15, C27, C55). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as standard efficient coding theory with appropriate acknowledgment of simplifications. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concerns that manuscript equates efficient coding with decorrelation, emphasizing decorrelation only maximizes information in absence of noise, and noting decorrelation and MSE minimization are not generally equivalent.

Both evaluate the block diagonal approximation assumption (C65-C66). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting the assumption's validity is uncertain and reasoning about weak correlations is plausible but indirect. Peer reviewers also rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly challenging this 'quite strong' and 'central' assumption in Round 2, noting objects are typically touched with multiple fingers, not one.

Both address background claims about sensory systems (C1-C3, C8-C11). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED as well-established findings with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not questioning these claims and implicitly accepting them through positive assessment that the problem is 'largely unexplored' with 'novel' results.

Both address literature background on density versus experience (C12-C14, C42-C46). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as accurate literature summary. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging these background claims while requesting clarification on how both factors contribute to the model.

Both address vision-related predictions and applications (C47-C49, C56-C57 for OpenEval; broader set C47-C59 for peer). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with reasonable bottleneck calculations and qualitative agreement. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging these discussion points and predictions though requesting clarification of underlying assumptions.

Both address developmental and aging changes (C50-C52). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as appropriate citations motivating potential applications. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED within broader discussion context (R10 includes C47-C59), not challenging these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses hierarchical magnification aspects (C53-C54) while peer R10 covers broader discussion including these claims. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate citations contextualizing model applicability. Peer reviewers rate their broader set SUPPORTED, not challenging these specific hierarchical claims.

OpenEval addresses tactile learning claims (C58-C59) while peer R10 covers broader discussion including these. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation. Peer reviewers rate their broader set SUPPORTED, not challenging these specific tactile learning claims.

OpenEval addresses prior theoretical work extension (C60) while peer R11 covers broader limitations/extensions (C60-C64). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable but untested inference. Peer reviewers rate their broader set SUPPORTED, not challenging this specific claim about prior work.

OpenEval addresses PCA generalization (C61-C62) while peer R11 covers broader limitations (C60-C64). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with sound argument for generalization. Peer reviewers rate their broader set SUPPORTED, requesting more explicit treatment of noise and nonlinearities but not challenging the PCA claims.

OpenEval addresses nonlinear model limitations (C63-C64) while peer R11 covers broader limitations (C60-C64). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as fair assessment of model scope. Peer reviewers rate their broader set SUPPORTED, requesting more explicit treatment but not challenging these acknowledged limitations.

OpenEval addresses mathematical structure of covariance function (C69) as straightforward and accurate. Peer R3 includes C69 within broader evaluation of density/activation effects (C39, C69, C71-C74) rated UNCERTAIN, requesting better explanation of how model treats these factors. The covariance structure itself is not directly challenged.

OpenEval evaluates the main conclusion (C7) as SUPPORTED by collective findings. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses this overarching claim, though peer concerns about specific components (theoretical framework, plasticity interpretation, empirical validation) indirectly affect confidence in the main conclusion.
